Subject: Elmwood Bank — priority gateway + residency ask (SOW attached)

Irene / Markus —

Quick context: Elmwood Bank (Samir Rao) came back from legal with an ask that will materially affect the commercial commitment. They want two things pinned for launch:

- A priority gateway (dedicated lane / pinning) that ensures sub-100ms p95 for their fraud-detection inference traffic, and
- Regional data residency in us-east with optional VPC-only access and a warm pool seeded at go-live.

They attach an initial SOW and asked whether we can deliver the priority lane and residency tradeoffs before they sign. They are willing to commit to a 12-month reserved capacity if we can guarantee the lane and an activation date within the next 6 weeks. I attached the SOW and a placeholder cost model.

Asking product/eng: is there a realistic short-term workaround we can offer (soft-priority lane + cache seeding) vs. a full pin/residency feature? If not, what is the engineering ETA and what tradeoffs (cost, token caps, fallbacks) should I present to the customer?

Next steps I need today: a one-paragraph decision we can share with procurement (Samir is pushing for dates).

Thanks —
Marissa

--

Subject: Re: Elmwood Bank — priority gateway + residency ask (SOW attached)

Thanks Marissa —

A few clarifying Qs before I draft a short decision:
1) Expected sustained QPS and peak concurrency for the fraud-detection workload? (ballpark is fine)
2) Are they insisting that the KV cache and logs never leave the us-east region, or is policy enforcement at control-plane level acceptable?
3) Who will sign (legal or procurement) and have they confirmed the 12-month commit level in $/month?

High level thoughts: a full “pinning” feature (reservation + strict affinity) is non-trivial and touches routing, admission control, and billing. A pragmatic short-term option is a reserved warm pool with pre-seeded cache and an SLA-backed soft-priority route (requests routed to the warm pool preferentially, with fallback to shared capacity). That should get us most of the latency benefits but still requires reserved capacity and some infra support for cache seeding.

Markus — can you flag whether the soft-priority + cache-seed approach is feasible as an interim deliverable (2 weeks to wire up routing + 1 week to validate)? If not, please provide an expected delivery window and a concise list of required infra changes.

I’ll hold off communicating to Samir until we have a one-paragraph option for procurement.

Irene
Director, Product Operations
irene_choi@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jul 2024 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Elmwood Bank — priority gateway + residency ask (SOW attached)

Short answer: interim path exists; full pinning is medium effort.

Details:
- Soft-priority lane + cache seeding: we can implement a routing policy to prefer a reserved warm pool (config flag) and seed the KV cache at activation. Engineering estimate: 2 person-weeks to add routing flag + 1 person-week for cache-seed tooling + 1 week for validation and runbooks (total ~4 weeks of calendar time if we allocate a focused squad). If we do a fast-track (small scope, holiday sprints) we can aim for ~2 weeks calendar with risk.

- Strict pinning / guaranteed residency (no cross-region control plane metadata): requires changes to routing fabric and additional KMS handling for regional keys. This is a larger infra project (6–8 weeks) and will require sign-off from infra and security.

Cost/Tradeoffs: the soft-priority approach requires reserved capacity (cost passed to customer). The warm pool seeding reduces cold-start latency but increases reserved GPU hours. Suggest we present two options to Elmwood:
  Option A (Fast): Soft-priority + warm pool (2 weeks optimistic / 4 weeks conservative). Requires 3x baseline reserved capacity for first 30 days to seed and stabilize.
  Option B (Full): Strict pin + regional KMS support (6–8 weeks) with higher engineering cost but lower long-term operational overhead.

I attached the draft cost model (cost_model.xlsx) and a short list of infra owners who will need to approve. If Marissa can confirm QPS and commit size we can produce a precise MRR number and a recommended activation date.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Group PM, Serving Runtime

He also wants the option for full pinning later in the year. Procurement will draft the PO once we give an activation date. Excerpt from Samir below:

On Mon, Jul 8, 2024 at 2:20 PM Samir Rao <samir@elmwoodbank.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — we can move forward on a 12-month reservation at the numbers you provided if Redwood can stand up the soft-priority lane and the warm pool within six weeks. The security team is okay with the residency model you described for now, as long as logs and PII stay in us-east. I will loop in procurement after you confirm an activation date.
>
> — Samir

Marissa here — we need an agreed short paragraph for procurement we can include in the SOW: something that says — we will provision a reserved warm pool in us-east and enable a soft-priority routing policy for Elmwood traffic; fallback to shared capacity if the warm pool is saturated; reserved capacity will be billed per the attached cost model; we target activation date X.

Monica — can you please prepare a 30/60/90 onboarding checklist and own the post-signing rollout? Ben — please include a legal contact for quick contract routing; they may push a short SLA line.

Irene / Markus — if you can provide the short paragraph plus a conservative activation date (we can give a range), I’ll ask procurement to circulate the PO.

Thanks —
Marissa
